rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 and Figs 2-3 report the authors' own operational mapping results (annual irrigated-area maps produced by their lab since 1998, time series 1982-2016 in Fig. 2) and a real plot case from the SPIDER-ERMOT tool (Fig. 3). Q2: Section 2 reports from the authors' project experience that the 1998 agreement between the J<U+00FA>car basin authority and the users' board led to annual maps used for water management, water rights assignment and sanctions; rights were regularized using the maps with about 95% agreement; a 2012 Supreme Court ruling set the conditions for satellite classification to count as evidence citing ERMOT; a Jury of Irrigation uses the SPIDER-ERMOT webGIS to resolve conflicts and sanction (Fig. 3 case); maps are posted on the CHJ website and shared by officials and farmers. Q6: Section 2 / Fig. 1 - the governance outcomes are reported for the whole Eastern La Mancha groundwater body (about 10,000 km2, ~100,000 ha irrigated), i.e. aquifer/basin scale. Q7: Section 2 states from the experience that sharing the base information (maps) between officials and farmer representatives is a crucial element for solving conflicts, and that the system rests on an agreement between the basin authority and the users' central board.
rows.notes: Conference 'lessons learned' paper, largely descriptive; evidence on governance/conflict resolution is narrative operational experience rather than a measured or surveyed outcome (the 95% agreement figure is attributed to ref [2]), so Q2 is a cautious yes. No triangulation, no measured mechanism, single aquifer, no dispersion measure. Stated limitations (no comparative analysis of water-meter vs crop-based allocation; need to explore non-adapted rules and law; further research on governance types and legal force) concern monitoring accuracy or future work rather than the governance result itself, so Q8 is no.

notes: Full text appears complete. The paper mixes a descriptive account of a 20-year operational programme with a methodological outline of RS-based water accounting; it presents no formal experiment or survey, so Q1 rests on the authors' own mapping products and case reporting.
